topic: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Homework
text:
Homework has traditionally been used to reinforce classroom learning, develop independent study habits, and evaluate student understanding. Generative AI has challenged this model because students can now obtain complete answers to many homework tasks within seconds. As a result, educators must reconsider the design and purpose of homework.

AI can support homework when used as a tutor. Students may ask for explanations, examples, hints, or feedback on their work. This assistance can be valuable when teachers or family members are unavailable. It may also help students overcome minor difficulties that would otherwise prevent them from completing an assignment.

However, AI can easily complete routine tasks on behalf of the student. Questions that require simple summaries, standard calculations, or predictable essays may no longer reveal what a student understands. A completed assignment may appear accurate even when the student has not engaged with the subject.

To remain meaningful, homework should focus on application, reflection, and personal reasoning. Teachers may ask students to connect ideas to classroom discussions, explain how they reached an answer, compare different approaches, or critique an AI-generated response. Assignments can also include drafts, notes, and brief oral follow-ups to show the learning process.

Educators should avoid assuming that all AI use is dishonest. Clear rules are more effective than vague prohibitions. Students should know when AI is permitted, what assistance must be disclosed, and which parts of the work must be completed independently.

AI does not eliminate the value of homework, but it reduces the usefulness of routine assignments. Effective homework in the AI era must emphasise thought, explanation, and application rather than simple answer production. The goal should be to make learning visible, not merely to collect completed work.
